content:
Most students treat quadratics as easy marks. Then a paper hides a common-root or location twist, and the clock wins. This free quadratic equation JEE mains online test fixes that gap. It gives 15 exam-pitched MCQs with instant scoring. Also, every answer carries a short worked reason. So aim for 12 out of 15, and note which idea trips you.

What JEE asks from quadratics

  • Nature of roots, and what the discriminant sign shows.
  • Sum and product of roots through the Vieta rules.
  • Common roots, so you subtract the two equations first.
  • Range of a quadratic, and the positive-for-all-x case.
  • Location of roots, because sign and vertex both matter.

Formulas to revise first

  • The discriminant is b squared minus 4ac, so its sign decides the roots.
  • Vieta gives the sum as -b/a, and the product as c/a.
  • Two quadratics share a root, so subtract them to find it.
  • A positive-for-all-x quadratic needs a above 0, and D below 0.
  • The vertex sits at x = -b/2a, and it marks the min or max.

Mistakes that cost JEE marks

  • The lead coefficient may vanish, so the equation can turn linear.
  • Writing only D below 0, and then dropping the sign of a.
  • Distinct roots need D above 0, but many settle for at least 0.
  • Chasing the real roots, when Vieta answers it far faster.

quiz.title: JEE Quadratic Equations Online Test
quiz.intro: Fifteen JEE-pitched questions on the discriminant, Vieta, common roots, range and location of roots. Pick an answer for each, then press Check my score.
quiz.about: Quadratic equations for JEE Main & Advanced

questions.q: If α and β are the roots of 2x² − 3x − 5 = 0, then α² + β² equals:
questions.explanation: By Vieta, α + β = 3/2 and αβ = −5/2. So α² + β² = (α + β)² − 2αβ = 9/4 + 5 = 29/4.

questions.q: The sum of the roots of 2x² − 7x + 3 = 0 is:
questions.explanation: The sum of roots equals −b/a = 7/2. The product c/a = 3/2 gives the roots 3 and 1/2.

questions.q: For what value of k does kx² − 2x + 1 = 0 have equal roots (k ≠ 0)?
questions.explanation: Equal roots need D = 0: (−2)² − 4k = 4 − 4k = 0, so k = 1. At k = 0 the equation is only linear.

questions.q: If x² + ax + b = 0 and x² + bx + a = 0 (a ≠ b) share a common root, then a + b equals:
questions.explanation: Subtract the equations: (a − b)x + (b − a) = 0, so x = 1. Put x = 1 into the first: 1 + a + b = 0, giving a + b = −1.

questions.q: If x² − 5x + 6 = 0 and x² − 3x + 2 = 0 share a root, that common root is:
questions.explanation: The first has roots 2 and 3, the second has roots 1 and 2. The shared value is 2.

questions.q: The minimum value of f(x) = x² − 4x + 7 is:
questions.explanation: For a > 0 the minimum is c − b²/4a = 7 − 16/4 = 3, reached at x = −b/2a = 2.

questions.q: If x² + bx + c = 0 has rational roots with integer b and c, which condition must hold?
options: b and c are both even.
questions.explanation: Rational roots need the discriminant b² − 4c to be a perfect square. That is the exact test for integer coefficients.

questions.q: If one root of x² − 5x + k = 0 is 2, the value of k is:
questions.explanation: Put x = 2: 4 − 10 + k = 0, so k = 6. The other root is then 3.

questions.q: Both roots of x² − 2mx + m² − 1 = 0 lie strictly between −2 and 4 for:
questions.explanation: The roots are m − 1 and m + 1. Need −2 < m − 1 and m + 1 < 4, so m > −1 and m < 3.

questions.q: If x³ − 2x² + 3x − 4 = 0 has roots α, β, γ, then α² + β² + γ² equals:
questions.explanation: Here α + β + γ = 2 and αβ + βγ + γα = 3. So α² + β² + γ² = 2² − 2(3) = 4 − 6 = −2.

questions.q: The solution set of x² − 5x + 6 < 0 is:
questions.explanation: The roots are 2 and 3. An upward parabola stays negative between its roots, so 2 < x < 3.

questions.q: x² − 2x + k = 0 has two distinct real roots when:
questions.explanation: Distinct real roots need D > 0: 4 − 4k > 0, so k < 1. At k = 1 the roots are equal.

questions.q: Both roots of 2x² − 5x + 3 = 0 lie in which interval?
questions.explanation: The roots are 1 and 3/2. Both sit inside the open interval (0, 2).

questions.q: One root of x² + px + 12 = 0 is 4, and x² + px + q = 0 has equal roots. Then q equals:
questions.explanation: Since 4 is a root of the first: 16 + 4p + 12 = 0, so p = −7. Equal roots need p² − 4q = 0: 49 = 4q, so q = 49/4.

questions.q: The roots of x² − 6x + 8 = 0 both lie in the interval:
questions.explanation: The roots are 2 and 4. Both lie inside the open interval (0, 5).

faq.q: Is this JEE Quadratic Equations online test free?
faq.a: Yes. All 15 questions, the scoring and the explanations are free. The e-book then adds daily graded problems with full solutions for Rs 49.

faq.q: Is the test JEE Main or Advanced level?
faq.a: Both. The set mixes JEE Main recognition questions with a few Advanced-style location-of-roots twists, so it stretches you without a huge time cost.

faq.q: Do I need to solve each quadratic to answer?
faq.a: Usually not. Vieta, the discriminant and location conditions answer most questions without finding the roots, which is exactly what saves time on the real paper.
Location of roots. It asks you to combine the sign of D, the sign of a·f(k) and the vertex position at once. A quick parabola sketch beats memorising cases.
